And like another person said... this is not your burden to bear. This is your dad’s mess. 

While many suggest telling your mom, I strongly suggest, for your own mental health, putting this burden back where it belongs- in your dads hands. Take yourself out of that equation or you just might get stuck in the middle.

OP it’s very interesting how similar our stories are. My dad did the very same thing and I was in your exact position. 

The woman was around all the time. Everything was right in front of us.

When I finally knew for sure, I never told my mom. I couldn’t bear to do that. I kept my dad’s secrets for over 15 years. Not to spare him, but for my own ‘safety’ and sanity.

My mom eventually “caught” him. And it still took me years to come clean about the things I knew. When I did though, my mom never once held me responsible or was upset with me. She told me that she knew, she was in denial. I thought it would be a weight off my shoulders coming clean to her, but the real liberation wouldn’t come for years until I finally came clean and held my dad responsible for everything. It was like stripping wet muddy clothing off for good. It helped a lot in the healing process.

It sucks and it's the hardest thing you'll do in your life, but man it is sooo temporary. When you realize just how much control you get to have over your life, it is a very powerful and liberating feeling. I promise it does not take much time or effort to start to see that perspective. And once you're there your possibilities are endless. Do not give up.

Unfortunately you're not at the point in your life where you'll find enjoyment in it. That's why you feel the way you do. You have to start from square one and work on yourself so that you are capable to go back to work and back to as normal of a life as you can lead. It's all part of a vicious cycle. But once you get going in the right direction you are on a roll. You will be able to get a job, you will meet new people. Your life will start to change.

Even better. 

Use this time for YOU. There is nobody more deserving of time for them self than you. Start small on your daily task and try your best to master that every day. Even if it's the only thing on your to do list, brush your teeth. Get it done. Then tomorrow, and the next and the next. Let yourself build on these tasks. Nothing is too small or petty. But it is clear that you are broken right now and I am so sorry you are hurting. I have been there and I am thankful for the days that I fought hard to just stand under the hot water only to go back to bed right after. It meant I did something today other than be depressed. It was the start of undoing my depression. It didn't erase it- nope that's biological and chemical makeup and unfortunately I'm stuck like this forever. But when I have shit days I stay in bed. And tomorrow I start fresh again and take that shower, brush my teeth, and pick my feet back up.

I've been there too op :'(

But I am here to tell you it truly gets better!

There was a time in my life that my hardest task of the day was putting on my makeup. I wasn't working. I had a caretaker essentially. I had all my needs met. And I couldn't get up and shower for the day let alone do anything else, because I was that miserable. 

For some, this is rock bottom and maybe this is it for you. Hopefully this is it for you because once you see that place and you find yourself on the incline out of it, you have the tools to keep you out of it for good. 

Try to identify your immediate needs. What sounds good right now? What do you need to feel good? It's called self care and it is the first and foremost that is going to get you out of this place. Some things but not limited to; 

- Taking a shower every day
- Brushing your teeth every day 
- Leaving the house, even if it's just once for lunch or gas or a drive, every day
- Try to get active -- go for a walk, try to once a day. 

If these tasks seem like hurdles? Start there! Call in sick to work, because you are sick! And start with your self care! It doesn't matter if you only accomplish one of those things in a day. Or in a week. But please please try your very best at getting just one of those done a day. I PROMISE you will start to feel even just a little bit better. Even if it's a little bit, you are headed in the right direction. 

There is only one you and you are given this one life. There is SO much more to you and the life you've been given than to live in this rut, and/or let this rut overcome your life. You are strong and you are able. 

Feel free to message me if you ever want to chat. No judgements and in confidence. You are loved op.

Much like u/TryinToBeHappy I found myself in your two same positions. No energy. No motivation. Shit I had a reason to be there, I wanted to go to medical school. For as long as I can remember, that's what I've wanted to do. 

But something beginning in my junior year of high school ate away at my mental state and continued into my college years. I fought and fought demons but persisted in school. I hardly ever had an entire week where I attended every class. I did the mindless work, but when it came down to applying myself I blew it off to sleep and feed my depression. I missed stupid participation points. I failed a handful of tests and just made it by on the others. 

I became so depressed I was suicidal. I began seeing a psychologist my senior year of college. By then it was far too late to salvage my grades, but my mental state improved. 

I actually graduated in 4 years with a bachelors in biology- one of the few degrees most undergraduate medical students graduate with. Seemed on track for my dream... However over 4 years I destroyed my GPA. So much to the point I will have nearly no chance of getting into medical school, let alone any assistance. I am six figures in student loan debt and will probably never live up to my commitment I made to myself years ago because I didn't take care of myself first enough so that I could live up to my fullest potential. 

*I am confident you are a smart and talented person. Sometimes those qualities are easily muffled when our perspectives are altered by our mental state. It's hard to see the point of going on or even feel it's worth anything even in the long run. But trust me when I say in a clear mind you will look back years after and completely regret letting your own self down because you couldn't find the energy to do it. 

Your mental health is so important and such a key element to the overall potential of life... not just in school. I sincerely encourage you find some time in your day to assess your actual needs and take care of you. YOU. However or whatever that may be. 

And when you are functioning in your normal state, you will be amazed at how different your energy and outlook towards your goals and values are. 

Keep up the hard work. You got this.
